live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): a social-engineering crew that goes after help desks
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST, better known as Scattered Spider, is a financially motivated group. Vendors say it tricks help desks and staff to get in, then steals data or deploys ransomware. Some links to other groups are only partly confirmed.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD HARVEST. The catalogue lists aliases including Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike describes SCATTERED SPIDER as a prolific eCrime adversary that has run financially motivated activity since early 2022.
Check Point Research, drawing on public intelligence, describes a group active since at least 2022. It says the members are mostly young people aged 19 to 22 from the US and UK.
ReliaQuest calls it a financially motivated gang associated with the hacking collective known as The Com.

In August 2025 a Telegram brand called Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters appeared. Trustwave SpiderLabs reads it as a situational alliance, not a formal merger. It infers from writing patterns that fewer than five people run the core.

EclecticIQ says there is no direct relationship between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider. Its analysts also assess that ShinyHunters very likely relies on Scattered Spider and The Com members for voice phishing.
CrowdStrike says the group's early campaigns reportedly hit customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms, plus telecommunications and technology companies.
ReliaQuest says 70% of the group's targets are in technology, finance and retail trade. Its figures come from a domain dataset and its own alerts.
Check Point says the group is widening its scope to aviation alongside enterprises. It cites media reports and advisories that link the group to airline attacks, including a July 2025 Qantas breach.

Google's John Hultquist, quoted by BleepingComputer, said the group has recently been breaching US insurers. An Aflac spokesperson could not name the group behind its breach, but the report says it shows all the signs of Scattered Spider.
Mandiant says UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
ReliaQuest says the group relies mainly on phishing, voice phishing and help-desk impersonation. It uses the Evilginx phishing framework to bypass MFA.
BleepingComputer's report on the Aflac breach lists phishing, SIM swapping and MFA bombing among the group's tactics.
Picus Labs says the group has been seen deploying commercial remote monitoring and management products. The catalogue lists AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein among its tools.
Google tracked a voice-phishing cluster, UNC6040, that tricked staff into linking a modified Salesforce data tool. Google ties its Okta phishing pages to Scattered Spider or The Com tactics.
Picus Labs describes an August 2025 Telegram post that sought insiders with Okta, Microsoft SSO or Citrix access.
ReliaQuest says the group has formed alliances with ransomware operators ALPHV, RansomHub and DragonForce, and increasingly targets managed service providers and IT contractors.
BleepingComputer's report says that in September 2023 the group breached MGM Resorts by impersonating an employee. It then encrypted over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors with BlackCat ransomware.
ReliaQuest says a wave of attacks hit UK retailers in May 2025, including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods. It says nothing definitive has tied those incidents to Scattered Spider.
Resecurity cites Scattered Spider ransomware attacks on WestJet, Hawaiian Airlines and Qantas in mid-2025. It does not believe the combined group's announced retirement is sincere.

Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Microsoft Teams message from a fake IT Support account. Rapid7 says the approach mirrors Octo Tempest-style tradecraft but does not confirm a link.
Help desks should confirm a caller's identity through a second, trusted channel before resetting MFA or passwords.
Staff should be trained to treat unexpected IT-support calls and chat messages with suspicion, including requests to install remote access tools.
